refuted_claims.claim: The task brief instructs: "Collect all units' `label_lookups`, then go further" — implying each of the nine agents left a label_lookups artifact to audit.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: No such artifacts exist. The nine units delivered output files only, so the label audit could not be done by reading their self-reports; it had to be reconstructed from scratch by diffing every unit's Chinese against a flattened lang/cn.json + lang/en.json en→cn map (548 unambiguous English labels).
refuted_claims.evidence: `find 6-工作区 -type f` returns exactly index.json, 6 .en.html, 6 .cn.html, SYS-I1/T1/U1.cn.json. Nothing named label_lookups anywhere under the project.

refuted_claims.claim: DO-NOT-TRANSLATE.json §exact_match_to_lang gives `lang_cn_shipped_by_upstream` for the 12 T-EXACT skill names: 机械 / 肉搏 / 射击 / 观察 / 操纵 / 科技 …
refuted_claims.why_wrong: That column is stale — it records the *upstream* system's cn.json, not the project's delivered lang/cn.json. Six of the twelve now differ. Anyone treating that column as the T-EXACT target would produce six wrong item names and silently break the skill-stunt panel on four sheets. The register's own `rule` field ("byte-equal to lang/cn.json's value") is the correct authority; the cached column is not.
refuted_claims.evidence: 1-系统汉化插件/lang/cn.json: SkillheavyMach=重型机械, SkillcloseCbt=近战, SkillrangedCbt=远程战斗, Skillobservation=侦察, Skillmanipulation=操控, Skillcomtech=通信科技. SYS-I1.cn.json matches lang 12/12 by repr() comparison (ok=12 bad=0).

refuted_claims.claim: DO-NOT-TRANSLATE.json records `ALIENRPG.CriticalInjuries` as `cn_shipped: "重伤"`, and RULINGS/glossary give Critical Injury = 重伤 — so a bilingual heading "重伤 Critical injuries" looks like a T-BILINGUAL violation on a lang-locked label.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The delivered cn.json ships ALIENRPG.CriticalInjuries as the English string 'Critical injuries', deliberately, via lang_keep_english.json (it is a live `game.tables.getName(localize(...))` leg). So the character/synthetic/creature sheets literally display "Critical injuries" in English. J2's and J3's "重伤 Critical injuries" headings are therefore *correct* — they name the section as the sheet names it — and the lowercase 'i' is intentional, not a broken frozen literal. My frozen-literal scan's "LOST" hits on 'Critical Injuries' in J2/J3/J6 are all this case plus two prose headings; zero are real.
refuted_claims.evidence: lang/cn.json ALIENRPG.CriticalInjuries = 'Critical injuries'; lang_keep_english.json keep_english list includes ALIENRPG.CriticalInjuries; templates/actor/character-general.hbs:249 and creature-general.hbs:17 render that key as the section label.

refuted_claims.claim: The brief's markup rules stress `@UUID[Item.<id>]{label}` byte-fidelity and `[[...]]` enrichers as the main markup risk for this corpus.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: This page contains none of either. The whole 66,228-char English page has 0 `@UUID`, 0 `@TEXTDRAW`, 0 `[[`, and 0 `data-hash`. That check is vacuous here; the real markup risks in this corpus are tag multiset, the `<span class="...">` image placeholders, and heading ids — all of which I verified separately.
refuted_claims.evidence: Assembled compendium/cn page: `data-hash in page: 0  @UUID: 0  [[: 0`. DO-NOT-TRANSLATE §heading_anchor_hashes independently measures system: data_hash_occurrences 0.

refuted_claims.claim: The prep script's own unit table names the SYS-J5 section 战斗轮 ("掷骰 / 生物 / 战斗轮 / 表格 / 系统设置 / 宏"), i.e. Combat Tracker = 战斗轮.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: 战斗轮 reads as "combat round" and collides head-on with the glossary's Round = 轮; the Foundry sidebar element is a tracker, not a round. The delivered text now uses 战斗追踪器 in both units that mention it. index.json's title string is an internal label and was not updated — flagging so nobody re-imports 战斗轮 from it in Phase 4/5.
refuted_claims.evidence: 4-常用脚本/parallel/prep_sys_units.py JOURNAL_UNITS SYS-J5 title; glossary_alien.json Round=轮; SYS-J5.cn.html and SYS-J6.cn.html now both read 战斗追踪器 ×3.

refuted_claims.claim: The nine unit outputs were a frozen snapshot to audit.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: They are not. SYS-J2/J3/J4/J5/J6 .cn.html were all rewritten on disk at 17:56:57 while this audit was mid-flight — between my first term-frequency pass and my second. That write silently fixed three defects I had already logged (J2 left `actor` untranslated ×4; J5 used 战斗轮 for Combat Tracker; J4/J5 used 点击). Every conclusion in this report was re-derived against the post-17:56 files. Anyone else auditing concurrently should assume the same hazard.
refuted_claims.evidence: mtimes: SYS-J2..J6 .cn.html = 2026-08-29 17:56:57; SYS-J1.cn.html = 17:31:49 (untouched). My own writes are 18:04:52 / 18:07:02 and are the newest on every file I edited.

verdict:
Assembly is clean and the pack is shippable; 9 fixes applied across 5 unit files, 8 items left open for the controller.

WHAT PASSED (all re-verified after my edits and after a concurrent 17:56 rewrite of J2–J6 that I had to re-baseline against):

• Markup, 6/6 journal units — tag multisets byte-equal to English (196/305/416/227/348/656 tags); every class=, style=, href=, src= identical in value and order; zero @UUID and zero [[…]] in this corpus, so those rules are vacuous here.
• Heading anchors, 91/91 — every heading carries an explicit id, and every id reproduces Foundry's slugifyHeading exactly. I reimplemented it against the real source (common/primitives/string.mjs:73 + journal-entry-page.mjs:76) including the 522-entry CHAR_MAP, so I could confirm the two hard cases: `&` → "and" (not "andamp") in the 3.3.2/3.3.0 headings, and the 64-char truncation on `version-4.0.3-added-the-consumables-to-the-evolved-character-she`. The CN page's 91-slug sequence is identical to the EN-derived sequence; the 6 duplicate slugs (general-tab, header-(1), details-(2), tracking-(3), armor, creatures) are pre-existing upstream, not regressions.
• 12 T-EXACT skill-stunt names — byte-equal to lang via repr(), 12/12, no English tails, no trailing spaces.
• Frozen literals, both directions — 0 violations. The only fields left identical to English in the three JSON units are exactly the ones that must be: 26 `[object Object]` notes, 3 RollTable names, 3 frozen folder names, and the Adventure name. `Alien Sub-Tables` → 异形子表 is correctly translated, `Alien Macros`/`Careers`/`Skill-Stunts` likewise. All 12 "LOST" hits from my frozen scan turned out to be correct behaviour (see refuted claim #3).
• Label fidelity — I rebuilt the audit from lang/en.json→lang/cn.json (548 unambiguous labels) and checked every one that occurs in the English. Item types match TYPES.Item.* 13/13; the crew roles, ranges, colony trio (政策/设施/工程 — note the third dropdown option is ALIENRPG.Projects, and J4 got that right), conditions, and settings labels all match byte-for-byte. Notable good calls: J5's “配置 Alien RPG 设置” = ALIENRPG.MenuLabel exactly; J1's 贴近距离 = ALIENRPG.Close, a key that has no English fallback at all; T1 reuses lang's Panic wording verbatim and preserves the table's own two-ASCII-space form (lang uses space+NBSP) plus the stray trailing apostrophe on row 7-7.
• Reassembly — `prep_sys_units.py --collect` passes: no MISSING, no UNTOUCHED, wrote 1-系统汉化插件/compendium/cn/alienrpg.alien-rpg-system.json, page 35,585 chars (en 66,228); folders 7/7, macros 4/4, items 26/26, tables 3/3, journal+page names left frozen at "MU/TH/ER Instructions.". Note this script writes compendium/cn itself — that is its designed behaviour, not me writing there.

THE ONE THING I'D ESCALATE: the macro-name split (missed_items #1). It is the only open item that is functional rather than stylistic — SYS-J5's Macros section instructs the reader to find four macros by names that SYS-U1 has renamed. Decide direction there before Phase 4/5.
